query: What are the real-world risks and benefits of using synthetic data to train or fine-tune large language models? Focus on data quality, bias, and evaluation.

sub_questions.text: How does synthetic data improve data quality for training large language models compared to real-world datasets?
Can synthetic data effectively reduce biases present in real-world training data for language models?
Under what conditions does synthetic data introduce new biases or fail to represent real-world diversity in language models?
What are the limitations of current evaluation metrics when assessing models trained on synthetic data?
How does the use of synthetic data affect the generalization performance of language models on real-world tasks?
